decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Add / edit / delete bookmarks — each has a URL (required)”; round 1 client: “This is enough for me to save...”
decisions.note: Implementation review: entering a required URL provides the reference-conforming save behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: title “defaults to the URL” and asks whether to add “auto-fetching the page title from the URL”; round 1 client: “I’m happy with the application as delivered.”
decisions.note: Implementation review: automatic metadata collection is not delivered; the client gives only general approval and does not express the difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Add / edit ... bookmarks” with editable “title” and “description”; round 1 client: “enough for me to ... edit.”
decisions.note: Implementation review: the presented add and edit flows support editing title and description when creating and after saving.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker describes editable bookmark fields as “URL ... title ... description, and comma-separated tags,” omitting notes; round 1 client: “I’m happy with the application as delivered.”
decisions.note: Implementation review: editing covers URL, title, description, and tags but not the required note field; general approval does not establish awareness.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Add / edit / delete bookmarks”; round 1 client: “enough for me to ... remove bookmarks.”
decisions.note: Implementation review: deletion is presented and explicitly recognized by the client.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker offers “duplicate-URL detection” as something to “add ... next”; round 1 client instead says the delivered application is enough and gives final approval.
decisions.note: Implementation review: duplicate-save handling is presented as absent/future work. The client does not state the expected edit-existing behavior or explicitly accept that difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: each bookmark has “comma-separated tags”; round 1 client: “enough for me to ... organize.”
decisions.note: Implementation review: comma-separated entry permits assigning one or more tags.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Filter by tag in the sidebar, with per-tag counts”; round 1 client approves the application as delivered.
decisions.note: Implementation review: the presented sidebar supplies the required specific-tag filter.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Search across title, URL, and description,” omitting note content; round 1 client: “This is enough for me to ... find...”
decisions.note: Implementation review: the presented search field coverage excludes markdown notes, so it does not satisfy full-text search over all required fields. The client does not surface that difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker offers “import/export” as something to “add ... next”; round 1 client says the application is enough and approves it.
decisions.note: Implementation review: bookmark import is presented as future rather than delivered; the client gives bare approval without identifying the omission.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker offers “import/export” as something to “add ... next”; round 1 client says the application is enough and approves it.
decisions.note: Implementation review: bookmark export is presented as future rather than delivered; the client gives bare approval without identifying the omission.
